The Rural Health Transformation Program is a rare example of taxpayer dollars being strategically redirected—not just spent. While $50B sounds steep, the key is how it's allocated: cutting bureaucratic middlemen and funding actual care. Compare that to Biden-era healthcare bloat, where billions vanished into admin costs and Medicaid fraud.

The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) proves targeted investment works when paired with accountability. Rural hospitals shouldn’t need $50B to function—they need Washington to stop strangling them with red tape and price-gouging contracts.

This funding’s a band-aid, but at least it’s applied to the right wound. Now let’s cure the disease: pharma monopolies, overpriced care, and D.C.’s addiction to complexity.
